source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Polity Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. What is a Constitution
points: A **Constitution** is the **fundamental (supreme) law** of a country — the set of basic rules by which it is governed.
It lays down the **structure of government**, the **powers** of its organs, and the **rights and duties** of citizens.
The **Constitution of India** is the world's **longest written constitution**.

sections.heading: 2. Making of the Constitution
points: Framed by the **Constituent Assembly** (1946–1949); **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** chaired the **Drafting Committee** ('Father of the Indian Constitution').
**Dr Rajendra Prasad** was President of the Constituent Assembly.
**Adopted on 26 November 1949**; came into force on **26 January 1950** (**Republic Day**).

sections.heading: 3. The Preamble
points: The **Preamble** is the introduction, stating the **ideals and objectives** of the Constitution.
It declares India a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic**.
It promises **Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity** to all citizens.
It begins with **"We, the People of India"** — power flows from the people.

sections.heading: 4. Key Features
points: **Fundamental Rights** — basic freedoms guaranteed to citizens (equality, freedom, against exploitation, religion, culture/education, constitutional remedies).
**Fundamental Duties** — responsibilities of citizens.
**Directive Principles** — guidelines for the government to promote welfare.
A **federal** structure (Union + States), a **parliamentary** system, and an **independent judiciary**.
The Constitution can be **amended** (changed) as society's needs change.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Constitution = fundamental/supreme law; India's is the longest written constitution.
Framed by the Constituent Assembly; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad = its President.
Adopted 26 Nov 1949; in force 26 Jan 1950 (Republic Day).
Preamble: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic; Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity; 'We, the People'.
Features: Fundamental Rights & Duties, Directive Principles, federal + parliamentary system, independent judiciary.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Constitution **adopted 26 Nov 1949**, but **came into force 26 Jan 1950** (Republic Day) — two different dates.
**Ambedkar** headed the **Drafting Committee**; **Rajendra Prasad** was **President of the Constituent Assembly**.
Preamble words to remember: **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic** (Socialist & Secular added later by the 42nd Amendment).
**Fundamental Rights** (justiciable) differ from **Directive Principles** (guidelines) and **Fundamental Duties**.
